market.series: ICE arabica benchmark (robusta series in assembly)

growing_conditions.location: Buon Ma Thuot, Dak Lak, Vietnam (12.68N, 108.04E)

crop.stage_note: harvest and sun-drying: excess rain delays picking and causes mold in drying yards — wetness is the risk, not drought
crop.method: 30-day rainfall anomaly weighted by the Dak Lak robusta phenology calendar (drought-sensitive flowering/fruit-set, wetness-sensitive harvest)

forecast.note: forward-looking model output; verified against realized rainfall in the public track record as windows close

brief: Coffee futures closed at 291¢/lb — up 4.4% on the week and down 11.5% on the month. The regime model reads the market as crisis and has for 14 sessions. Rainfall in the Central Highlands is running above its seasonal norm (+1.9σ) — favorable moisture for the robusta belt. The crop is in its maturation & harvest window, and stage-weighted stress is elevated. A weakening Brazilian real (+2.5% in a month) raises producers' local-currency revenue per bag — added selling pressure. Looking ahead: the 14-day forecast calls for 86 mm of rain in the robusta belt against a 146 mm seasonal norm (-0.4σ) — projected crop stress: low (Open-Meteo forecast model, issued 2026-10-03; skill scored publicly as windows close).
